description.narrative: Stödet syftar till att stärka och förbättra kvaliteten och relevansen i Tanzanias nationella forskningskapacitet att bidra till minskad fattigdom och Tanzanias hållbar utveckling. Målet är att förbättra forskningskapacitet och dess tillämpning på den största hälso-universitet och bidra i forskning för hälsa i huvudsak i områden med HIV/TBC, malaria, reproduktiv hälsa och hälsosystem

The support aims to strengthen and improve quality and relevance of the Tanzania national research capacity to contribute to poverty reduction and Tanzania's sustainable development. The objective is to enhance the research capacity and its application at the largest health university and contribute in research for helath mainly in areas of HIV/TBC, malaria, reproduct helath, health systems research.

Övergripande fråga: Resultat kopplat till avsedd effekt 2014Fråga: Sammanfatta resultat relaterade till avsedd effekt (denna information kommer att skickas till Open Aid).Svar: The objective of the program is to develop capacity within MUHAS that significantly will contribute to poverty reduction in Tanzania and Tanzania's Development Vision 2025 through multidisciplinary research in priority health areas and training of human resources in health research.
The support from Sida has contributed to the PhD training of 44/107 of MUHAS academic staff (41%). Already 46 percent of MUHAS staff has a PhD degree making it he lead instituion in health reserach in the country. MUHAS is the university (Scopus 2014) which generating the major part of scientific publications in Tanzania, not only in health but also compared with universities and research institutions in other areas.
MUHAS has also contributed to inform and influence laws and policy in diagnosis, prevention and treatment of transmitted diseases such as HIV/AIDS and malaria. It has also influenced policies in maternal and child health and a roadmap for reducing maternal and infant deaths. Focus areas of the research has been HIV vaccine trials, prevention of HIV from mother to infant, malaria drug efficacy and monitoring, drug administration of malaria infected HIV patients, malaria in pregnancy, child sexual abuse, rape and intimate partner violence, maternal health care. All research connected to national programs and policy.
During the year 42 scientific articles were published of which 36 in international journals. MUHAS is the institution in Tanzania which produces most scientific articles internationally showing high quality of the scientific outputs.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
